monitor.mechanism: Attack generation changes what a monitor is asked to recognize; a low conditional miss rate on one proxy can conceal weaknesses on another.
monitor.conditions: AISI fixes 25 IaC tasks and a retired GPT-5.4 xhigh monitor, with Qwen 3.8 27B xhigh. The monitor reads whole traces after completion; humans assign harmful side tasks. Optimization uses proxy monitors only.
monitor.counterexample: Basic attacks are usually detected and prompting/RL evasion transfers weakly to GPT-5.4 on LinuxArena. A failed proxy test is not a uniform failure across environments or monitors.
monitor.evidence: Read the original PDF §§1–4, Figure 1, Appendix B/Table 1 and Appendix F after the web PDF failed. Preserve conditional successful-side-task denominators, 95% bootstrap intervals and the distinction between maximum editing result and final budget.
monitor.limits: One agent and a stronger retired monitor, bounded task distributions and edited traces. Not present production behavior, pre-action blocking, overall attack success or benign false-positive rates; representative future attacks remain unknown.
monitor.mitigation: Justify and diversify test distributions, examine real failures and preserve independent permission controls, containment and human response. A low proxy miss rate alone is insufficient assurance.
monitor.readerContext: Read C3a1 in both languages alongside evaluation alternatives and the control tour. Define the population behind 0.2–23% and keep constructed task success separate from deployed failures.
monitor.whyHere: Add a controlled comparison of evaluation construction to C3a1, without changing its evidence level or claiming current monitors miss 23% of normal activity.

primary.support: Model pairing, held-out target monitor, conditional metric, uncertainty and limited cross-setting transfer.

audit.mechanism: Reading internal weight changes can reveal installed behavior that fixed output prompts fail to elicit, complementing output-based inspection.
audit.conditions: Sixty-eight LoRA adapters, including 58 with hidden behavior and ten benign controls; base weights available. Claude Opus 5.5 auditors and judges; 216 prompts, three runs per adapter and three evidence conditions.
audit.counterexample: The readout condition still misses behaviors and produces a majority-grade false positive on one of ten benign controls. Hidden-behavior success improves from 70/174 to 131/174, not perfect safety.
audit.evidence: Read Case study 1, Appendix C.2 and Table C2, plus discussion and unlearning comparison. Separate hidden-only denominators from all-adapter accuracy and benign majority grades; note reruns after cross-auditor file exposure.
audit.limits: Constructed finetunes, fixed questions, same-family AI grading and access to original/changed internals. Not an independently replicated deployment defense or measurement of pre-harm blocking.
audit.mitigation: Combine behavioral tests and internal audits with independently enforced permissions. Test unknown behaviors and false alarms before treating better identification as operational prevention.
audit.readerContext: Read C3a standalone in both languages and its alternatives. Introduce internal inspection in ordinary language before the card describes LoRA and the exact denominators.
audit.whyHere: Add measured defensive improvement to oversight while preserving existing misses, false positives and limited classification. Unlearning observations are review context, not a new sweeping safety claim.

primary.locator: Case study 1; Appendix C.2/Table C2; Discussion
primary.support: Audit conditions, access assumptions, 174 hidden-behavior audits per arm and benign controls.

work.mechanism: Technical capability translates into adoption through costs, workflows and organizational roles; hiring, substitution and complementary work can coexist.
work.conditions: Sixty-six interviews at 58 purposively selected US Anthropic customers, 25–40 minutes each, voluntary participation. No fixed assigned model or permissions; automated transcript coding and mainly qualitative self-assessed value.
work.counterexample: Reports of reduced hiring and contracting coexist with hiring more and redeploying staff. Useful AI does not require replacing every job, and unchanged employment does not mean no labor-market effects.
work.evidence: Read original report sections on sample, top-down automation and role reorganization, plus PDF Appendix. Publication is November 23; fieldwork dates are unspecified. Preserve respondents’ attribution rather than treating it as identified causality.
work.limits: Not representative of customers or the US economy; no causal net employment, productivity or household-welfare estimate. Proposed redeployment practices do not guarantee job security.
work.mitigation: Measure realized total costs, quality and worker outcomes; examine access to new jobs, skills and support. Treat role redesign as an observed/proposed response requiring evaluation.
work.readerContext: Read W3 and work-tour chapters in both languages, W4-W3 and all W3 outcome branches. Explain adoption first, then organizational conditions and divergent consequences.
work.whyHere: Add business-level adoption evidence to W3. Keep links to continued work, insufficient income and optional paid work conditional; no universal replacement or prosperity claim.

primary.locator: Summary; Introduction; Top-down automation; Reorganizing around AI; PDF Appendix
primary.support: Purposive sample, interview/coding method, self-reported hiring and work changes, limits.

control.mechanism: Preventing harm requires coverage, visibility, correct detection and timely authorized intervention. Detection after completion does not establish prevention before damage.
control.conditions: METR’s per-action monitor pauses flagged actions for human review but identifies coverage and authentic-approval gaps. New AISI tests inspect completed synthetic traces; internal auditing examines installed behaviors with weight access.
control.counterexample: Some dangerous cases are detected, independent containment can hold, and better internal inspection improves bounded identification. One monitoring miss does not imply irreversible or society-wide control loss.
control.evidence: Reread METR original monitoring argument and implementation gaps, complete C3 explanation and current evidence, and compare the new AISI and neuron results. Check C3-L joint conditions and ASI-C3 as conditional influence.
control.limits: No aggregate deployment safety rate, guaranteed prevention or permanent loss of control follows. Separate synthetic attacks, known incident replays, actual intervention and future hypotheses.
control.mitigation: Enforce permissions independently, verify coverage and genuine human authorization, and measure time to detection/blocking/recovery. Do not substitute retrospective detection for safe execution.
control.readerContext: Read control tour and oversight/evaluation graphs in both languages. C1, C2 and C3 remain joint conditions rather than sequential milestones; escalation beyond local harm requires more conditions.
control.whyHere: Substantively renew only due C3 and its matching evidence clock. Dependent control units are reviewed for consistency without refreshing their unrelated clocks or changing risk/evidence levels.

primary.locator: Structured monitoring argument; discovered issues; four conjunctive claims
primary.support: Coverage, visibility, detection and human review requirements.
Post-task proxy tests do not certify deployed prevention.

finance.mechanism: Financial disruption propagates only when important operations, buffers and containment/recovery fail together. Price changes alone do not establish functional collapse.
finance.conditions: FSB final practices distinguish controls on agents from fallback and common-provider continuity. The November 18 BCBS statement discusses correlated dependencies alongside broadly strong capital/liquidity.
finance.counterexample: Strong buffers, limits and recoverable critical services can contain shocks. A supervisory warning and an intended consultation do not demonstrate that systemic AI defenses have failed.
finance.evidence: Read FSB final report printed p. 53 and pp. 63–64, and the original November 18 BCBS statement linked in the companion record. Compare F4 with the F1/F2/F4 joint conditions for F3.
finance.limits: Practices and supervisory assessments are not measured AI-specific intervention effects or recovery rates. An announced future consultation is not an implemented or tested defense.
finance.mitigation: Test risk-based shutdown/override, independent fallback, recovery times, concentration scenarios and human authority. Track capital, liquidity and continuity separately.
finance.readerContext: Read F4 in both languages with finance-conditions, money tour and F1-F3. Keep operational/capital channels separate from claims about money disappearing or human extinction.
finance.whyHere: Retain the due F4 hypothesis and renew its clock after substantive review. No additional F4 current-evidence object is invented; dependent dates remain unchanged.

primary.support: Agent override/fallback and common-provider continuity recommendations, not measured effectiveness.

feedback.mechanism: An improved model must help the next development cycle, with validation and total costs compatible with continued progress, for a feedback loop to persist.
feedback.conditions: MASS uses two cycles in one model family with human-prepared tasks and training, with mixed benchmark results. METR Q4 examines public models and uncertain task/capability metrics; Phantom Gains supplies matched frozen controls in a different protocol.
feedback.counterexample: Some benchmarks do not improve; apparent gains can arise from repeat measurement. Conversely, lack of aggregate acceleration or a null in another protocol does not refute every possible recursive process.
feedback.evidence: Reread MASS v1 workflow transfer, training comparisons and discussion, METR Q4 overview/§3.C.2, and Phantom Gains measured-null comparisons. Compare both feedback-edge conditions with existing two-cycle and whole-process cost caveats.
feedback.limits: Output-token efficiency is not total search/training/human-cost efficiency or sustained whole-lab acceleration. New GPT-6.2 ChatGPT screening-based High designation does not demonstrate recursive acceleration.
feedback.mitigation: Use frozen controls, independent verification and whole-process costs across generations; preserve safety evaluations and restrict permissions before extending a development loop.
feedback.readerContext: Read both feedback connections and acceleration-tour context in Japanese and English. Separate observed local gains, a feedback relation and unbounded acceleration; no ASI date or probability is inferred.
feedback.whyHere: Retain R2-R3 and R3-R2 text, conditions and classifications after rechecking their evidence; renew only these due edge clocks.

primary.support: Two bounded cycles with gains and non-gains; output-token and whole-process distinctions.
Rapid measured capability growth without strong aggregate MCI acceleration in the sampled public frontier.
Limits of attributing repeated-test gains to actual self-improvement.

record.mechanism: An evidence update needs dated primary provenance, coherent dependent views and preserved prior records to remain reviewable.
record.conditions: Daily November 10–24 window; existing draft PR on a branch containing freshly fetched origin/main; root checkout untouched. Three sources/cards and three bilingual paragraphs, plus four due-item rechecks.
record.counterexample: An unchanged index, completed build or newer publication date alone cannot renew content clocks. New reports with overlapping claims can be screened without duplicate cards.
record.evidence: Read the full three new primary reports and relevant methods/limitations; compare new GPT-6.2 ChatGPT card and daily indices with existing sources. Companion Markdown lists decisions, IDs, URLs, limits and validation.
record.limits: Neither automated schema checks nor this editorial review establishes exhaustive coverage, independent replication or scientific certainty. Unknown experiment dates remain explicit.
record.mitigation: Preserve earlier sources/cards/history/translations and unrelated dates; validate both languages, review coverage, freshness, build and exact-head CI. Keep the PR draft for human review.
record.readerContext: Review new prose in standalone details and actual exported tours. Technical settings stay in evidence cards; no UI or glossary change is required for these additions.
record.whyHere: Record a bounded update and its dependencies without changing risk levels or causal topology. Update the existing PR, not duplicate it, merge it or deploy it.

primary.support: Qualitative adoption evidence and selection limits.
